messages:
Omar N: hey all, day 2 here. using Fedora + rootless podman for dev. host can curl internal grafana (10.12.9.40:3000) over corp VPN (OpenConnect), but from a rootless container i get DNS NXDOMAIN and trying to use the bastion socks proxy from inside the container fails. any pointers? :thinking:
Claire P: welcome Omar! quick checks: can you curl from host and from container? also paste `cat /etc/resolv.conf` on host and `podman run --rm --env=HOSTNAME busybox cat /etc/resolv.conf` output.
Omar N: host:
```
$ curl -v http://10.12.9.40:3000/health
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
host /etc/resolv.conf:
```
# Generated by NetworkManager
nameserver 127.0.0.53
search redwood.internal
```
container /etc/resolv.conf shows `nameserver 8.8.8.8` and search empty. ping by IP from container times out.
Ben I: rootless containers run in a user namespace and often get a different network namespace or a slirp4netns-managed network that doesn't inherit host routes or DNS. Two problems: DNS and routing to the VPN.
IT Ops: for DNS, because host uses systemd-resolved stub (127.0.0.53) the container can't reach that loopback. you can either: (A) pass `--dns=10.12.0.2` to the container, (B) configure Podman to use the host network plugin (`--network=host` works on linux non-rootless if rootless doesn't support it), or (C) bind mount the host resolv.conf into the container (risky). For routing, slirp4netns doesn't forward to tun0 by default. rootless podman has a `--net slirp4netns:allow_host_loopback=true` option which helps with host access.
Claire P: try this quick test from host:
```
socat TCP-LISTEN:31000,bind=127.0.0.1,fork TCP:10.12.9.40:3000 &
podman run --rm -p 31000:31000 --add-host=graf.local:127.0.0.1 curlimages/curl curl http://graf.local:31000/health
```
If that works the issue is the slirp network path.
Omar N: i tried binding socat and proxying, host curl -> OK, container -> times out. i started podman with `--net slirp4netns:allow_host_loopback=true` and added `--dns=10.12.0.2` and now DNS resolves but curl still times out trying to reach 10.12.9.40.
Ben I: two more things: 1) make sure OpenConnect is not in per-app mode; check `ip route` on host to confirm 10.12/16 is via tun0. 2) slirp4netns translates traffic through userland NAT which sometimes blocks hairpin to the VPN endpoint. Workaround: use SSH SOCKS from host and point container apps at it. On the host run `ssh -N -D 1080 $USER@bastion.redwood.com` then inside the container set `ALL_PROXY=socks5://host.containers.internal:1080` — but rootless networking may not let the container see host loopback.
IT Ops: more reliable: use `podman run --network=host` on a linux host (needs permission), or run a small proxy on the host bound to the host's LAN IP that the container can reach via slirp host loopback. Example host socat bind to the host IP (not 127.0.0.1):
```
sudo socat TCP-LISTEN:32000,bind=192.168.1.50,fork TCP:10.12.9.40:3000
```
Then in podman: `--add-host=graf.local:192.168.1.50` and curl graf.local:32000.
Omar N: i didn't think about binding to the host's LAN IP. my workstation IP is 192.168.1.50 — i tried socat bound to that and added `--add-host` and now container curl to graf.local:32000 returns 200! DNS + routing fixed by combining `--dns` and host-bound socat.
Claire P: excellent. we'll add a short note to the new-hires doc about rootless containers + slirp4netns and the two-step: add VPN DNS and use host-bound proxy or host network.
infra-bot: ticket INF-5320 created to add "rootless podman / slirp4netns + VPN" troubleshooting to onboarding docs (assigned eng-infra).
Omar N: huge help, thanks everyone :tada:
